newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Croatian PM seeks stronger ties in Malaysia visit.
newsitem.headline: Croatian PM seeks stronger ties in Malaysia visit.

text.p: Croatian Prime Minister Zlatko Matesa met Malaysian leader Mahathir Mohamad on Monday during a three-day visit aimed at strengthening ties.
Matesa arrived on Sunday leading a 12-member delegation of ministers and businessmen, the national Bernama news agency reported.

He was to visit Malaysia's Multimedia Development Corp Sdn Bhd, which is spearheading the development of the Multimedia Super Corridor (MSC), later on Monday. The MSC is a proposed information technology multimedia zone.
Croatia has agreed to permit Malaysia's Air Asia to fly to its capital Zagreb. National carrier Malaysia Airlines also has landing rights in that city.
Croatia also imports Malaysian-built Proton cars.
Follow-up discussions on air travel cooperation would be held between transport officials of the two sides, Bernama said.
Malaysian Foreign Minister Abdullah Ahmad Badawi told reporters that Prime Minister Mahathir assured the Croatian leader he would encourage private Malaysian companies to set up in that country.
The two leaders agreed that their countries should cooperate actively in areas such as power generation, shipbuilding and construction, Bernama said.
The volume of trade between the two stood at $5.12 million in 1994 and rose to $10 million last year, with the trade balance in favour of Malaysia.
